gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a two-shelf kidney corner lazy susan the kidney cut-out lines up with the cabinet opening only because of the pole's positioners. Rev-A-Shelf's 5472 manual says to screw the bottom positioner to the cabinet floor with the shaft locking screw facing the opening, then turn each shelf's positioner into alignment and lock it.
standout_why: I compared five pages. cabinetdata.com/lazy-susan-cabinet-dimensions already says a kidney's curved cut-out must clear the face frame and hinges, that kidney doors are usually mounted on the cabinet while pie-cut doors ride on the shelves, gives a 26–31 in pole range, and gives a 'smaller back-wall-to-opening measurement minus 2 in' diameter rule. tidystow's sizing guide gives 'narrowest opening minus 2 in', a 15–50 lb load range for home turntables and 18 in for most corner base cabinets. Lily Bearing's hardware guide gives steel bearing ratings (6 in = 500 lb) and says the bearing should be 1/3 to 1/2 of the top's diameter. None of them describes the positioner and locking screw, or the minimum-dimension figure in the maker's manual. Those pages already cover the alignment idea, though, so this finding adds only a little. simplehomenest's page is a product roundup with no fit facts.
decides: This doesn't change which product to pick. It confirms that a kidney unit like the Dowell or a Rev-A-Shelf 3472/5472 is right for a corner cabinet whose bifold doors are hinged to the cabinet. It adds one install check: the unit needs a cabinet floor to screw the bottom positioner into, and the shelves have to be indexed to the opening. The 11 in OXO tray needs only a clear opening of about 13 in (tidystow's 'minus 2 in' rule). For the Everbilt 6 in bearing, Lily Bearing's 1/3 to 1/2 rule limits the top to roughly 12–18 in, and Lily lists 15–30 in for a 6 in bearing. Dealectric lists no lazy susans or cabinet hardware, so this angle has nothing in the catalogue to link to.

findings.label: Minimum cabinet dimensions
findings.value: Manual: 'The dimensions shown in Figure 1. are minimum.' Figure values: 32 in, 28 in, 22-7/8 in, 21 in, 19-5/16 in, 18 in, 12 in, 11-1/16 in, 6-1/2 in, 5 in
findings.note: The page doesn't map each figure value to a dimension. 32/28 in matches the two shelf sizes.

findings.label: How the shelves are indexed to the opening
findings.value: Bottom positioner screwed to the cabinet floor with four 3/4 in #8 oval-head screws. 'Shaft locking screw must face cabinet opening.' Upper positioner set about 15 in from the bottom of the shaft, then 'Rotate the positioner and shelf into alignment' and tighten.
findings.note: Third-party copy of the maker's instruction sheet. The official PDF (images.salsify.com I-5472.pdf) downloaded but its text was compressed and couldn't be read.

findings.label: Door mounting by shape, and pole range
findings.value: Pie-cut: doors usually attach to the shelves. Kidney: doors usually mount on the cabinet and open on their own. Many telescoping shafts adjust about 26–31 in.
findings.source_title: What Lazy Susan Cabinet Dimensions Mean for Fit — Cabinet Data
findings.note: Rival page (rank 17 in chat 1, not cited). Listed to show this point is already covered.

findings.label: Maximum diameter rule
findings.value: Measure each back wall to the inside edge of the opening, take the smaller, and subtract about 2 in. Example: 34 − 2 = 32 in
findings.source_title: What Lazy Susan Cabinet Dimensions Mean for Fit — Cabinet Data

findings.label: Opening needed (sizing rule)
findings.value: Narrowest opening minus 2 in = maximum turntable diameter. An 11 in turntable needs about 13 in, and the guide's table pairs an 11 in opening or shelf depth with a 9 in turntable and a 14 in one with 12 in
findings.source_title: Lazy Susan Sizes: Size Chart, Placement, and Where They Fail – tidystow
findings.note: Rival page (rank 4 / rank 15). 11 + 2 = 13 in is my arithmetic from its rule.

findings.product: Everbilt 6 in. Square Lazy Susan Turntable 49548
findings.label: Top size a 6 in bearing supports
findings.value: Bearing should be about 1/3 to 1/2 of the top's diameter. For a 6 in bearing Lily lists 15–30 in tops and rates its own 6 in steel bearing at 500 lb
findings.source_title: Lazy Susan Hardware Guide: Size, Load & Selection (Lily Bearing)
findings.note: Lily Bearing's own product ratings, not Everbilt's. 6 × 2 = 12 in and 6 × 3 = 18 in are my arithmetic from the 1/3 to 1/2 rule. Rival page (rank 12 / 17).

findings.label: Hole pattern on a square two-plate bearing
findings.value: 'One frame has one hole in each corner and the other frame has two holes in each corner.' The top is fastened by driving a screw 'through the top into one of the smaller holes in the frame.'
findings.source_title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Installing Lazy Susan Hardware (Designs by Studio C, Cher-Ann, 2015-02-17)
findings.note: A blogger's build, not a maker's sheet. The bearing in the build isn't named as the Everbilt 49548.
